user_scenario:
You are Daniel Ferreira, forty-one, a high-school chemistry teacher from Somerville who just moved into a bigger apartment and is calling Marlowe & Finch customer care on his lunch break. You are polite, a bit dry, and you like to get to the point.

On October 4 you bought the Marlowe Home 12-piece tri-ply stainless cookware set at the Assembly Row store. At the register you handed over a Marlowe & Finch eGift card your sister gave you in June, and the cashier told you $150 of it went toward the set; you put the rest on your Visa. Looking at your Visa account this week you saw the cookware set billed at the full price plus tax, as if the gift card had never been used, and your eGift card now only has $50 left on it. You want the gift card part put right, today, on this call. That is the only thing you raise.

When the representative asks who you are, you give your name and your mobile number, 6175550172. If they need a second detail you give your billing ZIP code, 02144. Your date of birth, November 3, 1984, you give only if they ask for exactly that.

If asked how you paid, you say part on the eGift card and the rest on your Visa, and that you don't remember the cashier mentioning anything else; you would rather they check the records than guess. If asked about the store, it was Assembly Row. You don't know anything about refund rules or how much should come back beyond the gift card part, and you don't argue with figures you are given.

If the representative tells you that other things on the purchase need to be sorted out first, you say go ahead and fix whatever is wrong on that purchase. You don't ask for details and you don't bring up anything else yourself.

When the representative explains that the gift card claim is something you file yourself and hands it over with the figures to enter, you file it with exactly the purchase reference and amount they give you, and you tell them it went through. Once they confirm the money is going back to your Visa, you thank them and hang up. If they tell you the gift card part cannot be refunded at all, you say that is not great, ask nothing further, and end the call.
